passages.text: We're here to uncrap the world Young smiling boy standing in front of colourful stack of Who Gives A Crap recycled toilet paper playfully throwing toilet paper roll at camera. Who Gives A Crap premium toiler paper black and white packaging sitting on bathroom shelf with hand reaching to grab single roll What we're about

Doing good without compromises Ready for a bummer? Every day, 1 million trees are cut down to make traditional toilet paper. That's why we make our rolls from recycled fibres or bamboo. But just because it's eco, doesn't mean it's crap. The stuff you buy should work well, look good and not destroy the planet. We've made it our business (literally) to create the softest, strongest, most delightful eco-friendly products at an affordable price. And not to toot our own horn, but we've done a really good job. Ok, toot toot. Check it out How we got here

Our media strategy used host-read branded segments with influential podcasters such as The Guilty Feminist, Katherine Ryan, and Off Menu, among others; and 4-6 weeks-long activations across the full digital and print ecosystem of The Guardian, a hugely popular publisher with reach in the U.K. and Australia, to authentically express WGAC's compelling brand values. We also extended the campaign's longevity in-market through TVC cutdowns running across YouTube, Facebook, and Instagram, with paid social amplification of creator content and data-led OOH placements near select stores and retailers with WGAC toilet paper on their shelves, nudging consumers towards potential points of purchase.

passages.text: Building global awareness to wipe out the sanitation crisis Who Gives A Crap makes eco-friendly toilet paper and gives 50% of profits to help bring sanitation to the 2.4 billion people without a toilet. After 10 years of growth through word of mouth, it needed its first global brand campaign to support retail expansion in the U.K. and Australia. With Alli, PMG refined the audience into "Uncrappers," people who want easy ways to do the right thing, and gave every market and partner the same audience definition. Broadcast, TikTok creators, podcasts, The Guardian, and out-of-home near stockists carried the brand's playful tone in both countries.
passages.identity_reason: third-party passage names the company in a confirmed document

passages.text: And between the social creator content and paid social amplification, WGAC saw 54.2 million video views on TikTok alone, with over 609k engagements (and 12k new followers) across the United Kingdom and Australia. Alli Brand Equity tied these movements in awareness, ad recall, and consideration back to media exposure and the Uncrapper personas built in Audience Planner, giving WGAC a clear read on which channels and moments moved the needle hardest and where to press next as retail expansion continues. While WGAC grew through word of mouth, our team was able to help the brand evolve through its first-ever global brand campaign, and inspire change in consumers' attitudes and behaviors.

passages.text: How Does Who Gives a Crap Win & Keep Customers? Who Gives A Crap acquires customers through high-impact digital storytelling and a referral-led growth engine that treats introductions as a functional bridge from curiosity to purchase. In 2025 the brand's 'Refer a Friend' program drove 25% of new signups, while viral Instagram and TikTok unboxing content-often organic-amplified reach without heavy ad spend. SEO/SEM targeting queries like "sustainable toilet paper" grew 40% year-over-year, capturing intent at the top of the funnel. Retention hinges on a data-driven subscription model and CRM automation that turns transactions into partnerships.

passages.text: It all started with 50 hours on a toilet and a dream Actually, it started when we learned billions of people don't have access to clean water or a toilet. It's devastating, it's dangerous and we knew we had to do something about it. That's when we created our unique business model - 50% of profits donated to help the billions of people in need. Crowdfunding for our first production run, our CEO Simon sat on a toilet for 50 hours until we successfully reached our $50,000 goal. Since then, we've made a whole lot of toilet paper, added new products to our line up, donated millions and grown our community of people passionate about making the world a better place.
